purpose: Small diagnostic pilot; not a representative benchmark or causal proof of retrieval advantage.

tasks.prompt: Write only Jac source for walker CollectEnabled. The harness already declares node Item with name: str and enabled: bool = True; do not redeclare Item. The walker is spawned at root and must follow all outgoing edges through a finite tree of Item nodes. Collect names only from enabled Item nodes, but continue traversal through disabled ones. Emit exactly one report containing the collected names sorted alphabetically, including an empty list when nothing matches. Declare a typed report channel. Repeated spawns must not share collection state. Do not mutate graph nodes. Return only the walker declaration, without Markdown or demonstration code.
expected_concepts: typed walker has fields and independent defaults
Root entry, Item entry, Root exit
here versus self
visit statement continues graph traversal
accumulate then report once; list-of-list report channel
manual_constraints: Uses walker abilities and traversal rather than graph-inspection helpers.

tasks.prompt: Write only Jac source declaring obj InvoiceLine. It must have required fields sku: str and unit_price: int, quantity: int defaulting to 1, and tags: list[str] defaulting to a fresh empty list per instance. Declare subtotal: int as a computed post-initialization field equal to unit_price times quantity. Callers must not need to pass subtotal. Preserve an explicitly supplied tags list. All fields must be typed and declared; use Jac constructor generation and postinit rather than a Python __init__ or embedded Python. Quantity zero is valid. Return only the object declaration, without Markdown or demonstration code.
expected_concepts: required fields before defaulted fields
typed has declarations and automatic constructors
mutable defaults per instance
postinit field exclusion from constructor
def postinit initializes derived fields
manual_constraints: Uses postinit field and method, not a property or custom constructor.

tasks.prompt: Write Jac function rank_scores(scores: dict[str, int], minimum: int) -> list[str]. Return names whose scores are at least minimum, ordered by descending score and then ascending name for ties. Support empty dictionaries and negative scores. Leave the input dictionary unchanged. Build the eligible entries by iterating over scores.items() with tuple unpacking, and use sorted with a typed Jac lambda as the sort key. Return only the function and any required standard-library imports, without Markdown or demonstration code. Do not use embedded Python.
expected_concepts: parenthesized tuple unpacking in for loops
typed parenthesized lambda parameters and brace bodies
tuple sort keys for descending score and ascending name
dict and list generic annotations
inclusive filtering without input mutation
manual_constraints: Uses sorted with a typed Jac lambda key.

tasks.prompt: Write complete Jac module date_math.jac containing days_between(start: str, end: str) -> int. Inputs are ISO calendar dates YYYY-MM-DD. Return end minus start in days, preserving negative differences and handling leap years correctly. Invalid dates must raise ValueError. Use an explicit selective import from Python datetime and its date parser; do not hand-code calendar arithmetic or embed Python. The module must print exactly "date helper ready" when run directly, but must print nothing when imported by another Jac module. Return only the module source, without Markdown.
expected_concepts: selective brace imports without trailing semicolon
explicit Python stdlib imports
typed function parameters and return
guarded with entry:__main__ versus import-time with entry
stdlib date arithmetic and ValueError propagation
manual_constraints: Uses selective datetime import and date parser.
Uses guarded Jac entry, not argv/path inspection.
